item.title: Wednesday Weather: Storms on the way! - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Mary Apel
item.description:
Happy Wednesday morning! It’s another day to stay weather aware.

We’re looking at a very active forecast, with rain possible throughout the day and thunderstorms becoming more numerous this afternoon and into the early evening. Some storms could turn severe, especially in the highlighted Enhanced Risk areas, with damaging winds, large hail from quarter-size up to golf ball-size, and even tornadoes all possible. A Level 2 Slight Risk has also been added for parts of South Mississippi and northeast Louisiana.

Highs will climb to around 78 degrees, but don’t let the warm temperatures fool you: this could be a rough weather day at times. In addition to severe storms, localized flooding will also be possible where heavy rain sets up.

Tonight, scattered thunderstorms will continue and may become more widespread overnight before tapering later, with lows around 60. Some stronger storms could linger into the evening hours, so keep a way to get weather alerts, especially after dark.

And this unsettled pattern isn’t going anywhere just yet. More rain and storms are expected Thursday and Friday as well. Bottom line: have the umbrella nearby, have a way to get warnings, and stay alert through today and tonight.

item.title: Study: Three Mississippi towns rank among most envied middle-class lifestyles - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
TUPELO — Three Mississippi communities — Tupelo , Oxford and Madison — are drawing national attention as places where residents say the middle-class lifestyle still feels within reach, according to a new survey on the most “envied” places to live.

The study, conducted by Calgary Homes and based on responses from more than 3,000 people, ranked cities across the country where Americans believe they can achieve a balance of affordability, community and quality of life. While no Mississippi city cracked the top 10, Tupelo ranked No. 49 nationwide, followed by Oxford at No. 82 and Madison at No. 97.

The results highlight a shift in what Americans value, moving away from ultra-wealthy enclaves and toward places where everyday life feels both comfortable and attainable.

Tupelo, best known as the birthplace of Elvis Presley, stood out for its strong sense of community and ongoing investment in local amenities. The survey pointed to a revitalized downtown, improved parks and schools, and a culture where neighbors look out for one another as key factors driving its appeal.

In Oxford, home to the University of Mississippi, respondents cited the city’s blend of culture and tradition. Its walkable Square, lined with bookstores, boutiques and locally owned restaurants, was noted as the social center of a town where college-town energy meets a slower-paced Southern lifestyle.

Madison, a suburb north of Jackson, earned recognition for its schools, low crime rate and family-oriented atmosphere. The survey described it as the kind of place where residents prioritize safety, education and day-to-day quality of life, with neighborhoods that emphasize stability and community connection.

Nationally, Colorado Springs, Colorado, topped the list, followed by St. Augustine, Florida, and Hilo, Hawaii, all locations that combine natural beauty, economic opportunity and livability without the extreme costs of larger metropolitan areas.

The survey suggests that while Mississippi’s cities may not dominate national headlines, they are increasingly part of the conversation about where Americans believe a fulfilling, middle-class life is still possible.

A spokesperson for Calgary Homes said the findings reflect a broader change in how Americans define success.

“For most people, the idea of ‘making it’ hasn’t disappeared, it’s just evolved,” the spokesperson said. “The most envied places aren’t about excess or status, but about balance: strong communities, access to nature and a lifestyle that feels attainable.”

item.title: Ridgeland Police to host community blood drive for Cpl. Ryan Stacy - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RIDGELAND — The Ridgeland Police Department is asking the community to donate blood during a drive next week in support of an officer seriously injured in a crash.

The community blood drive for Cpl. Ryan Stacy is scheduled for May 6 from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m. at the Ridgeland Police Department.

Stacy was seriously injured April 26 in a crash along the Natchez Trace Parkway when his vehicle struck a fallen tree during severe weather. He remains on what the department has described as a long road to recovery.

Police said donating blood is one of the most meaningful ways the public can support Stacy and others in need.

Officials said donations made ahead of the drive can be credited using the code ES24.

The department said the blood drive is intended not only to support Stacy, but also help meet broader community medical needs.

Police have thanked the public for an outpouring of support for Stacy and his family since the crash.

item.title: Preparedness through annual specialized emergency training at MSFA - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
PEARL — The Chlorine Institute is on site this week at the Mississippi State Fire Academy for a week of intensive CHLOREP Team Training, delivering hands‑on, scenario‑based instruction for participants, primarily emergency response contractors and CI member personnel.

The 2026 training includes a record‑breaking 129 students, supported by more than 70 experienced instructors, making it one of the largest CHLOREP Team Training events conducted at MSFA. Participants are engaged in realistic exercises designed to prepare response teams for the unlikely event of a chlorine emergency, with a strong emphasis on responder safety, technical proficiency, and coordinated decision‑making.

This year also marks 20 years of CI conducting CHLOREP training at MSFA, reflecting a long‑standing partnership focused on strengthening emergency preparedness and response capability.

CHLOREP Team Training is a core component of CI’s emergency preparedness program and supports emergency responders nationwide through specialized, hands‑on education. This year’s training includes international students from Puerto Rico, Mexico, Canada, and Trinidad and Tobago, alongside responders from across the US.

About The Chlorine Institute

The Chlorine Institute is a technical trade association comprised of over 200 member companies dedicated to the safe and responsible production, transportation, storage, handling, and use of chlorine and related substances. Chlorine is an essential element used worldwide to protect public health, support critical infrastructure, and enable the production of everyday goods. CI advances safety and stewardship through education, guidance, and emergency response preparedness.

About CHLOREP

Launched in 1972, CHLOREP is CI’s mutual aid program that provides a rapid and effective response to chlorine emergencies in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico by ensuring that transportation service providers, end-users, first responders, hazmat teams and others have quick access to accurate information and industry expertise.

The Chlorine Institute exists to support the chlor-alkali industry in advancing safe, secure, environmentally compatible and sustainable production, distribution and use of its mission chemicals: chlorine, sodium and potassium hydroxides, sodium hypochlorite, the distribution of vinyl chloride monomer and the distribution and use of hydrogen chloride. Visit us online at: www.chlorineinstitute.org.

item.title: New state-of-the-art radiation oncology systems offer advanced cancer care at UMMC - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
By Annie Oeth University of Mississippi Medical Center

JACKSON – Patrick McCarthy is fighting squamous cell carcinoma with the help of new advanced radiotherapy systems at the University of Mississippi Medical Center’s radiation oncology center, part of the UMMC Cancer Center and Research Institute.

The two new Varian systems, Edge and Ethos, offer patients faster, more precise radiotherapy. The Medical Center has the only Ethos system in Mississippi. The state-of-the-art system uses artificial intelligence for adaptive radiation therapy, which allows for adjustments in real time.

After a 13-day hospital stay, McCarthy, of Jackson, is undergoing radiation therapy as well as chemotherapy for squamous cell carcinoma, the most common type of tonsil cancer. He is among the first patients in Mississippi to receive radiotherapy with the Ethos system.

McCarthy came to UMMC after coughing up blood.

“My wife was in Memphis for our oldest daughter’s baby shower,” he said. “When she got home, she drove me to emergency care. She asked where I wanted to go, and I said, ‘Take me to the university.’ It’s been one of the best decisions I’ve ever made. The care I’ve had has been incredible.”

The Edge model at UMMC, accurate to a fraction of a millimeter, is the most advanced stereotactic radiosurgery system available in Mississippi when combined with its onboard surface-guided imaging system.

Stereotactic radiosurgery is a non-invasive, highly precise radiotherapy that targets tumors using 3D imaging and high-dose radiation.

The Medical Center has the only Ethos system in Mississippi. The state-of-the-art system uses artificial intelligence for adaptive radiation therapy, which allows for adjustments in real time.

“If a tumor shrinks or moves, adjustments are made to reduce radiation exposure for healthy tissue and minimize side effects,” said Dr. Neil Duggar, associate professor of radiation oncology.

On-table imaging can be done in six seconds, and radiation treatments on the new systems are shorter, Duggar said.

Dr. Rojymon Jacob, chair of the Department of Radiation Oncology, said those advances add up to treatments that better target tumors.

“When you combine real‑time imaging, adaptive planning and sub‑millimeter accuracy, you give patients safer treatments, more options, and a better chance at the outcomes they deserve. This is the level of cancer care Mississippians should have access to, and we’re proud to deliver it.”

The advancements, in a newly renovated space at University Hospital, come as a new five-story cancer center is on the drawing board. Radiation Oncology clinic appointments are now at CCRI’s location in the UMMC Medical Pavilion.

CCRI isn’t waiting for the new cancer center to be built to offer world-class care, Duggar said. “We have the most advanced radiotherapy treatment systems in the state now. We didn’t want to wait. The time to elevate the level of care is now.”

“Greater accuracy reduces exposure to healthy tissue and allows for higher doses of radiation in shorter periods and can even mean fewer treatments for some patients,” he said. “This is leading to better outcomes and new treatment options.”

Both systems can treat tumors anywhere on the body.

Dr. Rod Rocconi, Ergon Chair for Cancer Research and CCRI director, said the new radiotherapy treatment options reflect the level of care at CCRI.

“Mississippians deserve the most advanced cancer care available right here at home,” he said. “These advancements are already changing what’s possible for patients and families across our state.”

The renovated location at University Hospital will be home to radiation oncology treatment until the opening of the new center. Funded in part by It’s About Time: The Campaign for the UMMC Cancer Center and Research Institute, a $125 million philanthropic drive, the building will combine advanced, evidence-based care and research.

item.title: Meth, guns and vehicle seized in Tishomingo County drug raid - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TISHOMINGO COUNTY – Three people were arrested Sunday after a narcotics search warrant was executed at a residence on Highway 25 south of the Iuka city limits, according to the Tishomingo County Sheriff’s Office.

Authorities said the warrant was served April 26 following what the sheriff’s office described as an extensive investigation by its Narcotics Division with assistance from the Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics.

During the search, deputies seized about 65.1 grams of methamphetamine, equipment used to distribute narcotics, five firearms, various drug paraphernalia and a vehicle that authorities said was being used to transport drugs.

Manda Lynn Daniel was arrested and charged with three counts of sale of methamphetamine enhanced within 1,500 feet of a church, trafficking methamphetamine and possession of drug paraphernalia, according to the sheriff’s office. Judge Jeff Sparks set her bond at $200,000.

Christopher Shawn Clark was arrested and charged with possession of methamphetamine between one-tenth and 2 grams and possession of drug paraphernalia. His bond was set at $5,000, authorities said.

Christopher Lane Reno was arrested and charged with possession of drug paraphernalia. Judge Sparks set his bond at $1,320, according to the sheriff’s office.

item.title: Lowndes County deputies seek help locating fugitive wanted for embezzlement - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LOWNDES COUNTY – The Lowndes County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help in locating a Columbus man wanted for embezzlement.

Authorities identified the fugitive as 30-year-old Michael Miller of Columbus.

The sheriff’s office featured Miller in its latest “Warrant Wednesday” notice and asked anyone with information about his whereabouts to contact the Lowndes County Sheriff’s Office or Golden Triangle Crime Stoppers.

Tips can also be submitted anonymously through the T3 Tips app, according to authorities. The sheriff’s office said tipsters may be eligible for a cash reward if the information leads to an arrest.

item.title: JSU announces new ‘Jubilee’ opera inspired by famed author Margaret Walker Alexander - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
JACKSON — The Margaret Walker Center and Department of Music at Jackson State University announce the inaugural HBCU Opera and Musical Theater Summer Festival. The festival will debut a new folk opera entitled ‘Jubilee,’ inspired by the 1966 novel written by esteemed scholar Dr. Margaret Walker.

A series of grants will support the festival at JSU from June 7-14, 2026, and a concert production of the opera at Yale University on May 28, 2026. Funding will provide stipends for students and artists, cover travel costs, rehearsals and more.

“We are so excited to continue to expand the academic, artistic and activist legacy of our founder, Margaret Walker Alexander. Jubilee is a seminal work of fiction that launched an entire genre of neo-slave narratives. Now, with a new opera, ever more audiences will be introduced to this timeless piece,” said Director of the Margaret Walker Center Robert Luckett, Ph.D.

In 2025, the MWC was awarded a $25,000 grant by the National Endowment for the Arts (NEA) and another $125,000 after being recognized as a Yale Alliance for Scholarship, Collaboration, Engagement, Networking and Development (ASCEND) Initiative partner through Yale University. JSU’s Director of Opera and Musical Theater Phyllis Lewis-Hale, D.M.A., also secured a $20,000 grant from the NEA.

Additionally, a $100,000 grant to support cultural and civic engagement was secured from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), thanks to Almesha L. Campbell, Ph.D., vice president for research and economic development.

Award-winning composer and pianist Randy Klein, as well as librettist and playwright Joan Ross Sorkin, have developed the folk opera in conjunction with the MWC, which aims to capture the vernacular of the time period the opera is set. Klein and Sorkin are tasked with transforming the “Jubilee” novel, from the rich narrative to the complex dialect of its characters, into a powerful musical. Internationally acclaimed award-winning conductor and composer Julius P. Williams will lead the symphonic interpretation of the music.

Through the lens of Walker’s great-grandmother Vyry’s journey from slavery to freedom, the opera will bridge the struggle for equality and civil rights across the 19th and 20th centuries. It will also incorporate poems from Walker’s “This is My Century,” dated in the 1960s, infusing song with narration.

“We think this partnership is exactly the thing that Margaret Walker would be applauding, because she was a great civil rights advocate, and she was a great person to try to integrate all people together, to be able to do things together,” said Sorkin. “She was not trying to create fissions between groups. She really was someone who wanted to bring people together. And I think this project is such an exemplar of that. And I think it’s pretty thrilling.”

According to Hale, the week-long festival is modeled after and a continuation of the inaugural S.O.S (Summer Opera/South) Boot Camp held in February 2025. It will feature students from JSU, Fisk University, Xavier University of Louisiana, Alcorn State University and Tougaloo College, providing them an opportunity to learn from industry professionals, get firsthand interpretive coaching and work with Klein and Sorkin leading up to the debut of ‘Jubilee.’ The boot camp was led by Hale.

“The collaboration with Dr. Luckett and Opera/South is building upon students at Yale and HBCUs learning about Margaret Walker, the Margaret Walker Center and understanding the importance of this historical icon that is Margaret Walker,” said Hale. “The students became very excited about that. They’re excited about getting a chance to see what students at Yale will feel learning about Margaret Walker, reading Jubilee and really getting into the depth of the story.”

Hale and colleagues hope to host the festival annually across the nation, in collaboration with Yale and various institutions, while further expanding the ‘Jubilee’ concert into a full-scale production.

item.title: Jackson hair salon wins appeal after model claimed photos used without permission - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — A Mississippi appeals court has thrown out a $50,000 judgment against a Jackson hair salon, ruling that a woman who claimed the business used her photos without permission actually agreed to the arrangement all along.

Ada Green sued salon owner Latrice Rogers in 2022, saying Rogers put photos of Green on billboards, flyers and vending machines to advertise her hair extension business — Goddess of Great Lengths — without ever getting Green’s consent or paying her for it. A Hinds County jury sided with Green last August and awarded her $150,000. Judge Adrienne Wooten later cut that to $50,000.

But the Mississippi Court of Appeals reversed the judgment Monday, saying Green’s own behavior told a different story than her testimony.

The court pointed to Green’s social media posts, where she had celebrated seeing herself on billboards and described herself as a “brand ambassador” for the salon, the same role she denied holding in court. She also admitted she never once asked Rogers to take the photos down during the roughly six years they were in use.

Rogers testified that Green not only agreed to the photo shoots but personally chose which pictures went on which marketing materials. Two other witnesses backed that account.

Green said she only participated because it was part of her job, and that she posted about the salon on social media because Rogers made her.

Under Mississippi law, Green had to prove Rogers used her image without her consent. The appeals court said she didn’t come close to proving that, and threw the case out entirely.

One judge dissented but did not explain why.

JACKSON — A Mississippi appeals court has thrown out a $50,000 judgment against a Jackson hair salon, ruling that a woman who claimed the business used her photos without permission actually agreed to the arrangement all along.

Ada Green sued salon owner Latrice Rogers in 2022, saying Rogers put photos of Green on billboards, flyers and vending machines to advertise her hair extension business — Goddess of Great Lengths — without ever getting Green’s consent or paying her for it. A Hinds County jury sided with Green last August and awarded her $150,000. Judge Adrienne Wooten later cut that to $50,000.

But the Mississippi Court of Appeals reversed the judgment Monday, saying Green’s own behavior told a different story than her testimony.

The court pointed to Green’s social media posts, where she had celebrated seeing herself on billboards and described herself as a “brand ambassador” for the salon, the same role she denied holding in court. She also admitted she never once asked Rogers to take the photos down during the roughly six years they were in use.

Rogers testified that Green not only agreed to the photo shoots but personally chose which pictures went on which marketing materials. Two other witnesses backed that account.

Green said she only participated because it was part of her job, and that she posted about the salon on social media because Rogers made her.

Under Mississippi law, Green had to prove Rogers used her image without her consent. The appeals court said she didn’t come close to proving that, and threw the case out entirely.

One judge dissented but did not explain why.

Corrections officers, investigators and patrol deputies immediately pursued Hall as law enforcement established a perimeter in nearby wooded areas, roadways and highways.

Authorities said Hall was found and taken back into custody around 3 p.m. with assistance from K-9 Amos.

According to the jail’s website, Hall faces multiple charges, including:

Multiple agencies assisted in the search, including the Mississippi Highway Patrol K Troop, Mississippi Department of Corrections , Picayune Police Department , Poplarville Police Department and the United States Marshals Service , along with several other agencies.

item.title: Greenville crews clear more than 30 fallen trees after severe thunderstorm - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GREENVILLE – City crews in Greenville have removed more than 30 fallen trees following a severe thunderstorm, according to Mayor Errick D. Simmons.

In a statement issued Wednesday morning, Simmons urged residents to remain cautious as recovery efforts continue across the city.

The mayor thanked Public Works crews, first responders and emergency personnel for responding overnight to storm-related damage.

Simmons said cleanup work is still underway and asked residents to be patient as crews continue clearing debris and addressing issues citywide.

Residents who encounter downed limbs, blocked streets or other hazardous conditions are encouraged to report them to the appropriate city department, the mayor said.

“Storms may test us, but they also remind us of the strength and resilience of our community,” Simmons said. “We will continue working until the job is done.”

He also urged residents to stay safe, remain alert and give city crews grace as they work.

item.title: Court won't reconsider DUI conviction in deadly Hinds County crash - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — A Mississippi appeals court has refused to reinstate a drunk driving conviction it threw out earlier this year against a woman whose impaired driving killed a mother and child in 2021.

The Mississippi Court of Appeals denied the state’s request for rehearing Monday without explanation in the case of Beth Ann White, leaving in place its earlier decision to overturn one of her five DUI convictions.

White was convicted in Hinds County Circuit Court in 2024 on all five counts stemming from a November 1, 2021, crash that killed two people and seriously injured two others.

Allison Conaway and her six-month old son, Alex, were killed in the crash and her two daughters were critically injured.

The appeals court upheld four of those convictions but threw out a fifth, a repeat-offender DUI charge, ruling that prosecutors added it too late under the state’s two-year statute of limitations.

Attorney General Lynn Fitch’s office had asked the court to reconsider, arguing that White’s arrest on the day of the crash started the clock on the entire prosecution, including the repeat-offender charge. The court declined Monday to revisit that ruling.

White remains convicted on the four aggravated DUI counts. The case was tried in Hinds County Circuit Court before Judge Winston Kidd.

item.title: Walmart in Wiggins evacuated after ruptured gas line - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
WIGGINS – The Walmart Supercenter in Wiggins was evacuated early Monday after a ruptured gas line was reported outside the store, according to the Wiggins Fire Department.

Firefighters responded at about 3 a.m. to the store after reports of a gas line rupture.

When crews arrived, they confirmed the damaged line was outside the building and had been accidentally struck, the fire department said.

As a precaution, the store was evacuated.

The fire department said the Walmart Supercenter will remain closed until the gas line is repaired and the area is declared safe by the local gas company.

Wiggins Fire Department units remained on scene and on standby while repairs were underway.

Officials said Walmart will resume normal operations once the repairs are completed and the scene is cleared.

item.title: Tuesday Weather: Mix of clouds, possible storms - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Mary Apel
item.description:
Happy Tuesday morning, friends! It’s going to be a warm and somewhat unsettled day across the area, with highs climbing to around 82 degrees. Expect a mix of clouds and sunshine this morning, with isolated thunderstorms developing this afternoon. A few of those storms could turn strong to severe, so keep an eye on the sky if you have outdoor plans. South winds will be breezy at 10 to 15 mph.

Tonight, thunderstorms remain possible through the evening before tapering off after midnight, leaving behind mostly cloudy skies and a mild low near 68 degrees. Some storms could still be strong early on.

Looking ahead, we stay in an active weather pattern for much of the week. More scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms are possible Wednesday, then cooler air moves in Thursday with more clouds around.

Friday looks to be the wettest day of the stretch, with widespread rain likely and much cooler temperatures, only reaching the low 60s. A few leftover showers are possible Saturday morning, but the weekend improves nicely, with sunshine returning Sunday and temperatures rebounding into the mid-70s.

Overall, expect a stormy start to the week, a cooler and soggy finish to the workweek, and much nicer weather by the weekend.

item.title: Ridgeland PD asks public to help injured officer - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RIDGELAND — The Ridgeland Police Department is asking the public to help out an officer who was seriously injured in a crash along the Natchez Trace Parkway during severe weather Sunday morning, officials said.

Cpl. Ryan Stacy was involved in the crash April 26 when his vehicle struck a fallen tree on the Natchez Trace, according to the police department.

Authorities said Stacy had to be extricated from the vehicle and was taken to a local hospital, where he is being treated for serious injuries.

Police Chief Brian Myers said the department is asking for prayers for Stacy and his family as he recovers.

“The Ridgeland PD family asks for your prayers for a speedy recovery for Ryan and prayers for his family during this difficult time,” Myers said in a statement.

The department said Stacy faces a lengthy recovery and asked the community to keep him, his family and fellow officers in their prayers.

Stacy was recently recognized as Officer of the Month during the department’s March board meeting.

Support efforts for Stacy and his family are being coordinated through the 1828 Project of Madison County, according to the department.

item.title: National LawFit Challenge returning to DeSoto County in July - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
DESOTO COUNTY — Some of the nation’s fittest law enforcement officers will return to north Mississippi this summer for the 2026 National LawFit Challenge , a three-day competition focused on fitness, discipline and professional camaraderie.

The event is scheduled for July 16-18 in DeSoto County and will bring together officers from across the country to compete in a series of physical challenges designed to test strength, speed, flexibility and endurance.

The competition is hosted in Mississippi in part because of the state’s long-standing success in the event, according to Thomas Tuggle, the national LawFit coordinator. Founded in 2002, the competition has become a showcase for law enforcement fitness and preparedness.

Participants compete in events including bench press, pull-ups, sit-ups, a 1.5-mile run and a 200-yard agility course that simulates job-related tasks such as suspect apprehension, officer rescue, wall climbs and simulated shooting.

Tuggle has said the event promotes health, better decision-making and survival readiness for officers in high-risk situations, while also fostering friendships among competitors.

“It’s designed to test strength, speed, flexibility and endurance,” Tuggle said in past years. “They leave there with a newfound idea of what friendship is.”

Organizers say the competition highlights leadership and discipline while encouraging officers to set fitness goals and push themselves professionally and personally.

Mississippi has long fielded strong competitors in the event, with Tuggle previously saying the state’s performance helps counter stereotypes about law enforcement in the state.

Registration is now open for competitors, and organizers are also seeking sponsors for the 2026 event.

item.title: Mississippi joins multistate human trafficking operation that led to 4 arrests, recovery of 3 victims in Biloxi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
BILOXI – Mississippi participated in a nationwide human trafficking operation spanning 30 states that led to four arrests and the recovery of three victims in Biloxi, according to Attorney General Lynn Fitch.

Fitch said the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office Human Trafficking Task Force led the state’s role in Operation Coast to Coast, which was conducted April 23.

Nationally, the operation involved more than 250 law enforcement agencies and resulted in 59 arrests and the recovery of 166 victims, including 12 minors, according to the attorney general’s office.

“My office is committed to taking criminals who traffic people off our streets and equally committed to setting victims on the road to recovery,” Fitch said in a statement. “Developing partnerships with federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies both within Mississippi and across the country is a priority for the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office.”

The attorney general’s office said agencies involved in Mississippi included the Biloxi Police Department, FBI, Harrison County Sheriff’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations, Mississippi Bureau of Investigation and Mississippi Gaming Commission.

The Gulf Coast Center for Nonviolence provided services and treatment to the victims recovered during the operation, according to the attorney general’s office.

Operation Coast to Coast began in 2024 as an initiative of the Human Trafficking Training Center to encourage a broader national response to human trafficking, officials said.

The attorney general’s office said it has now trained 588 law enforcement officers statewide. It also said the office’s human trafficking team has led 63 multi-jurisdictional operations resulting in the recovery of 390 victims and 204 arrests, along with additional leads tied to trafficking investigations.

item.title: Mississippi Blood Services asks for platelet donations - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
FLOWOOD — Mississippi Blood Services is calling for immediate platelet donors as inventory has dropped to critically low levels, raising concerns about meeting patient needs statewide.

Officials said the organization needs to collect at least 40 platelet donations daily to supply partner hospitals across Mississippi.

Platelets are used to help control bleeding and support patients undergoing cancer treatment, major surgeries and emergency care. Because platelets expire within five days of donation, officials said maintaining a steady donor base is crucial.

“We need to collect 40 or more platelet donations daily to adequately supply our local hospital partners,” Kasey Dickson, the organization’s director of marketing and public relations, said in a statement.

Dickson said sickle cell patients and cancer patients of all ages rely on platelet products to continue lifesaving treatments.

“Without enough donors, those treatments — along with critical surgeries — can be delayed,” Dickson said.

Mississippi Blood Services is encouraging eligible donors to give as soon as possible. As an incentive, platelet donors will receive a $50 Visa gift card.

Donations are being accepted at the organization’s centers in Flowood, Cleveland and Oxford. The Flowood donation center, located at 115 Tree St., offers weekday and weekend hours, including Sunday appointments for platelet donations only. Centers in Cleveland and Oxford are also accepting donors during scheduled weekday hours.

Appointments can be made through Mississippi Blood Services or by phone, though walk-in donors are also welcome. Officials said additional donors are needed immediately to help prevent disruptions in care.

item.title: Mississippi Attorney General K9 Trace to Get Donation of Body Armor - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Today, Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced that K9 Officer TracE will receive a bullet and stab protective vest thanks to a charitable donation from non-profit organization Vested Interest in K9s, Inc. K9 TracE’s vest was sponsored by Eve R. Hershkowitz of Brielle, NJ and will be embroidered with the sentiment “Gifted by Eve R. Hershkowitz, Brielle, NJ”. Delivery is expected within ten weeks.

“Providing protective equipment to K9s like TracE ensures that our law enforcement dogs receive the same level of protection as the officers they serve alongside,” said Attorney General Fitch. “This donation will allow TracE to not only work effectively and confidently in high-risk situations, but ensure her safety and wellbeing when engaged in law enforcement activities. Thank you to Vested Interest and Ms. Hershkowitz for their generous gift.”

Vested Interest in K9s, Inc., established in 2009, is a 501(c)(3) charity whose mission is to provide bullet and stab protective vests and other assistance to dogs of law enforcement and related agencies throughout the United States. This potentially lifesaving body armor for four-legged K9 officers is U.S. made, custom fitted, and National Institute of Justice (NIJ) certified. Since its inception, Vested Interest in K9s, Inc. has provided over 6,397 vests valued at $6.9 million to K9s in all 50 states, made possible by both private and corporate donations.

The program is open to U.S. dogs at least 20 months old, actively employed, and certified with law enforcement or related agencies. K9s with expired vests are also eligible to participate. There are an estimated 30,000 law enforcement K9s throughout the United States.

Vested Interest in K9s, Inc. accepts tax-deductible contributions in any amount, while a single donation of $1,050 will sponsor one vest. Each vest has a value of $1,800.00, weighs an average of 4-5 lbs., and comes with a five-year warranty. For more information, or to learn about volunteer opportunities, please call (508) 824-6978. Vested Interest in K9s, Inc. provides information, lists events, and accepts donations at www.vik9s.org , or you may mail your contribution to P.O. Box 9, East Taunton, MA 02718.

You can learn more about Mississippi Attorney General K9 TracE by visiting attorneygenerallynnfitch.com/divisions/cyber-crime/ .

item.title: MHP investigates hit-and-run crash involving Lafayette County school bus - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LAFAYETTE COUNTY – The Mississippi Highway Patrol is investigating a hit-and-run crash involving a Lafayette County School District bus and a passenger vehicle on Highway 334, according to the Lafayette County Sheriff’s Department.

Deputies were dispatched to the crash at about 3:32 p.m. Monday, April 27, authorities said.

The sheriff’s department said the driver of the passenger vehicle left the scene before deputies arrived. No injuries were reported.

The Lafayette County Fire Department, Lafayette County Emergency Management Agency and Baptist Ambulance Service also responded to the scene, according to the release.

Investigators said the Mississippi Highway Patrol is leading the investigation with assistance from Lafayette County sheriff’s investigators. Authorities said detectives have identified a person of interest, but no name has been released.

Sheriff Joey East said the case will be pursued aggressively.

“The safety of our children and the men and women who drive them to school every day is non-negotiable,” East said in a statement. “In Lafayette County, there will be zero tolerance for anyone who puts our students or our bus drivers in harm’s way.”

No additional information was immediately released.
